<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl`

```text
1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
5	# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
6	# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
7	# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
8	# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
9	# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
10	# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
11	#
12	# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
13	# new contents on stdout.
14	#
15	# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
16	#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
17	#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
18	#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
19	#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
20	#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
21	#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
22	#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
23	#
24	# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
25	# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
26	# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
27	# round-trips both.
28	#
29	# Note: the template is written to a temp file via a heredoc *redirect* (not
30	# captured with $(...)), because the config body contains a lone backtick
31	# (`key = "prefix+\`"`) that bash mis-parses as command substitution when a
32	# quoted heredoc is nested inside $(...). Passing the path to Python sidesteps it.
33	#
34	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
35	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
36	# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
37	# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
38	# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
39	set -eu
40	
41	tmpl_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/herdr-config.XXXXXX")
42	trap 'rm -f "$tmpl_file"' EXIT INT TERM
43	
44	cat <<'TOML' > "$tmpl_file"
45	{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}

52	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then

86	# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.
87	try:

89	except ModuleNotFoundError:
90	    print(
91	        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
92	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
93	        file=sys.stderr,
94	    )
95	    emit_template()
96	    sys.exit(0)

98	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
99	
100	live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()
101	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
102	live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
103	
104	# Pull through every top-level key herdr owns at runtime that we don't manage.
105	for key, value in live.items():
106	    if key in MANAGED or key in doc:

42	#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
43	#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
44	# NOTE (herdr >=0.7.x): with "follow", a NEW TAB inherits the FOCUSED pane's live

46	# splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root" was treated as a bug and
47	# removed. NO new_cwd value opens a new tab at the WORKSPACE ("space") dir — for
48	# that use the prefix+C command below (derives the space root → tab create --cwd).
49	# See docs/tools/herdr.md.

51	
52	# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
53	# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything
54	# not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings (herdr docs), so a
55	# single action can carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
56	[keys]
57	split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
58	split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
59	reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
60	rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
61	new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)
62

64	# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; add the workspace + agent analogs
65	# so a number key jumps directly, no navigate mode needed. The "N..M" range form
66	# is native herdr config syntax (same shape as switch_tab).
67	# NOTE on the modifier: prefix+SHIFT+digit does NOT work — under the kitty
68	# keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) shift+1 still carries the printable "!", so
69	# herdr matches the symbol, not "shift+1". ctrl+digit and alt+digit have no
70	# printable form, so they disambiguate cleanly. Hence ctrl (workspace) / alt (agent).

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>

 `./docs/tools/herdr.md`

```text
1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **`modify_` overlay** (`dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` + managed body in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`). The overlay enforces our managed tables on every `chezmoi apply` while preserving whatever herdr writes back at runtime (see [Config management](#config-management-why-modify_)).
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Model differences vs tmux
19	
20	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
21	
22	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
23	
24	### Named sessions
25	
26	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
27	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
28	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
29	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
30	
31	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
32	
33	## cwd & workspace-naming model
34	
35	herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
36	
37	- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
38	- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
39	- **New tabs follow the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x).** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *new tab* inherits the focused pane's live cwd — same as a *split*. herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) changed `follow` so tabs behave like splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root (often `$HOME`)" was treated as a bug and removed. There is **no `new_cwd` value** (and no workspace-level cwd — `herdr workspace get` exposes none) that opens a new tab at the workspace root; for that use **`prefix+C`** (below).
40	- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.
41	
42	**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
43	
44	| value | meaning |
45	|---|---|
46	| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
47	| `home` | `$HOME` |
48	| `current` | herdr's **own process** directory (NOT the focused pane) |
49	| `"~/path"` | a fixed path |
50	
51	**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.
52	
53	```toml
54	[[keys.command]]
55	key = "prefix+C"
56	type = "pane"
57	command = "~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
58	description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"
59	```
60	
61	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
62	
63	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
66	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
67	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
68	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
69	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux) |
70	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
71	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
72	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
73	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
74	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
75	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | Partial — `report-metadata --custom-status` (per-pane, orthogonal to agent state) | **Review-pending flag** (`hmark`/`prefix+m` + `tv herdr-review` inbox); decorative status-bar glyphs still a gap (no format-string interpolation) |
76	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
77	
78	## Keybindings
79	
80	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
81	
82	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
83	
84	| Key | Action | Type |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
87	| `prefix + C` | new tab at the workspace (**space**) root dir — `prefix+c` + mouse "+" stay follow-focused-pane | command pane |
88	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
89	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + %` · `prefix + minus` / `prefix + "` | split side-by-side / stacked (tmux muscle memory — both the intuitive key and the tmux default) | rebound (arrays) |
90	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
91	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |
92	| `prefix + ctrl + 1..9` | jump directly to **workspace** N (`switch_workspace`) | rebound (indexed) |
93	| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | jump directly to **agent** N's pane (`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |
94	
95	> **Why ctrl/alt, not shift, for the indexed jumps**: under the Kitty keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) `shift+1` still carries the printable `!`, so herdr matches the symbol rather than `shift+1` — `prefix+shift+1..9` silently does nothing. `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` have no printable form and disambiguate cleanly.
96	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
97	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
98	| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
99	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
100	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
101	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
102	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
103	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
104	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
105	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
106	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
107	| `prefix + m` | toggle **review-pending** flag (⭐) on the current pane | command pane |
108	| `prefix + i` | `tv herdr-review` — review-pending **inbox** (flagged panes) | command pane |
109	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
110	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
111	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
112	
113	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
114	
115	## Session helpers: `hvibe` / `hcode` / `hhere` / `hroot` (herdr analogs of `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot`)
116	
117	Four shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) are the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot` helpers. The two **heavyweight** ones (`hvibe` / `hcode`) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion; the two **lightweight** ones (`hhere` / `hroot`) just open a plain workspace at a directory and attach — no git repo, no agent layout. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse the pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.
118	
119	| Command | Builds workspace | Layout |
120	|---|---|---|
121	| `hvibe [N] [CLI]` / `hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode` | `vibe/<repo>` | tab `agents` (N even-width agent panes) + tab `git` (lazygit) + tab `edit` (nvim) |
122	| `hvibe --tab-per-agent …` | `vibe/<repo>` | one tab **per agent** + `git` + `edit` tabs |
123	| `hcode [CLI]` | `coding-agent/<repo>` | tab `editor` (nvim 75% \| agent 25%) + tab `monitor` (btop) |
124	| `hhere [CMD...]` | `<basename $PWD>` | single tab, plain shell at `$PWD` (or `-p DIR`); optional `CMD` in the root pane |
125	| `hroot [CMD...]` | `<basename git-root>` | same as `hhere` but at the current git root (falls back to `$PWD`) |
126	
127	- **The plain-open pair (`hhere` / `hroot`)** fills the gap where every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent layout. With tmux, `tmux new-session` lands you in `$PWD` directly; herdr adds a Workspace layer, so without these you'd launch herdr, create a space (which opens at `$HOME` per `new_cwd`), then `cd` by hand. `hhere` does the one-shot: `herdr workspace create --cwd "$PWD"` → focus → attach if outside. No git requirement; the optional command runs **raw** (no specstory/on-exit wrapping — that stays with `hcode`/`hvibe`). `hhere -h` / `hroot -h` for flags. **Label caveat**: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to its root pane's *live* cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see the **cwd & workspace-naming model** section above), so the idempotent-focus is best-effort — a drifted label makes a re-run open a fresh workspace.
128	- **Idempotent per repo**: re-running focuses the existing `vibe/<repo>` / `coding-agent/<repo>` workspace instead of duplicating (matches svibe's "attach if exists").
129	- **Attach-aware (like svibe's `$TMUX` branch)**: run from **inside** herdr → the workspace/tab focus calls switch the live client (no new client). Run from a **plain terminal outside** herdr → the helper brings up a client attached to the session so the new workspace is actually visible (herdr's `workspace focus` only moves an *already-attached* client, so without this the pack was built invisibly). `--no-attach` builds detached either way. Detection is the ambient `HERDR_ENV`.
130	- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
131	- **Agent visibility**: herdr tracks agent state **per pane**, so in the default splits layout every agent still surfaces individually in herdr's agent tracking (verified: two agents in one tab appear as two separate entries in `herdr agent list`). The compact left sidebar rolls a *tab's* status into one dot — use `--tab-per-agent` if you want each agent to own a tab-level status dot.
132	- **Even columns**: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so `hvibe` sets each split's `--ratio` explicitly (`1/(N-m+1)`) to keep the agent panes even; `hcode` uses `--ratio 0.75` to give nvim 75%.
133	- Same flags as svibe/scode: `--on-exit`, `--no-specstory`, `--no-attach`, `-p/--path`, plus `--session NAME`; `hvibe` also takes `--min-width` / `--tab-per-agent` and honors `$HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` / `$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER`. Full flag help: `hvibe -h` / `hcode -h`.
134	
135	The tmux `svibe` / `scode` remain the tmux-side equivalents (see [sesh](sesh.md)); the two families coexist — `hvibe`/`hcode` only touch herdr, `svibe`/`scode` only touch tmux.
136	
137	## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)
138	
139	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).
140	
141	**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:
142	
143	```bash
144	herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
145	```
146	
147	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
148	
149	Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
150	
151	## Television integration
152	
153	Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Three ship here:
154	
155	- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
156	- `herdr-agent-panes` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`) — same source as `agent-panes`, but switch/kill use `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`.
157	- `herdr-review` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml`) — the **review-pending inbox**: lists only panes carrying the ⭐ flag (`custom_status ~ REVIEW`). Enter focuses the pane's workspace/tab and **keeps** the flag; `Alt+C` focuses **and** clears it ("mark read"). Bound to `prefix+i`. See the **Review-pending flag** section below.
158	
159	The original tmux-bound `sesh` / `agent-panes` channels are left intact for coexistence.
160	
161	## Agent state (replaces the 6-file workmux integration)
162	
163	herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
164	
165	```bash
166	herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --agent claude --state working
167	```
168	
169	For the trial we rely on native detection — the tmux-side workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system (Claude/OpenCode hooks → `@workmux_status`) is untouched and only applies under tmux.
170	
171	### Optional agent integrations (the onboarding "install" button)
172	
173	herdr's first-run onboarding offers to **install optional agent integrations** (`herdr integration install <agent>`), so agents report state directly instead of relying on screen heuristics. Pressing *install* sets these up for every detected agent. What it writes (verified on this machine):
174	
175	| Agent | What `herdr integration install` creates | Touches a repo-managed file? |
176	|---|---|---|
177	| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
178	| codex | `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` only | No — `~/.codex/config.toml` is untouched (identical to the chezmoi-computed target). |
179	| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` (separate plugin) | No — only `workmux-status.ts` is managed; herdr's plugin coexists. |
180	| cursor | `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh` + hook | Script lives outside chezmoi; coexists. |
181	
182	These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
183	
184	### Config management (why `modify_`)
185	
186	herdr can rewrite `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` at runtime — finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime.
187	
188	This file was originally seeded once with the `create_` prefix so `chezmoi apply` wouldn't clobber that writeback. The cost: **repo edits never reached an already-seeded machine** — split-key rebinds and comment fixes made in the source silently never arrived without a manual `cp … source-path` refresh. That is the real reason a host could feel "out of sync" while `chezmoi diff` showed clean (the diff was clean *because* `create_` never re-touches the file). Note this is independent of hosts: `chezmoi diff` of the source against each host's live file can be byte-identical yet a repo edit still won't land until you refresh.
189	
190	It is now a **`modify_` overlay** — `dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, a small script that:
191	
192	- uses the managed body in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` as the base (comments + tmux-parity rationale), enforcing the `[theme]` / `[ui]` / `[terminal]` / `[keys]` tables on every apply, and
193	- **pulls through every other top-level key** the live file has (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, …) so herdr's runtime writeback survives.
194	
195	TOML has no `jq`, so the merge runs in Python via `uv run --with tomlkit` (tomlkit round-trips comments **and** the `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables; stdlib `tomllib` is read-only and the codex `modify_` emitter can't emit AoT). It degrades to system `python3`, then to emitting the raw managed template, so a fresh host without Python still gets a full config. Second TOML-overlay precedent alongside `~/.codex/config.toml` (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`).
196	
197	To change herdr's managed config, edit `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` and `chezmoi apply` — it now reaches every host. Validate with `herdr server reload-config` (reports keybind collisions in its `diagnostics`; an empty `diagnostics` array + `"status":"applied"` means the config — including array key bindings — parsed clean).
198	
199	## Persistence & restore (accidental close)
200	
201	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
202	
203	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
204	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
205	
206	## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
207	
208	herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
209	
210	```bash
211	herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
212	herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
213	```
214	
215	What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
216	
217	- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
218	- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
219	- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
220	
221	**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
222	
223	- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
224	- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
225	
226	**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
227	
228	```bash
229	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
230	```
231	
232	If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
233	
234	## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
235	
236	The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
237	
238	Three ways to resolve it, in order of preference here:
239	
240	1. **Double-prefix passthrough (recommended, zero config).** tmux keeps its default `bind -T prefix C-b send-prefix` (confirmed present in this repo — not overridden), so **`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b`** forwards a literal `Ctrl+b` to the inner herdr; its prefix bindings then work normally (`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b c` = inner new tab). No herdr or tmux change needed — classic tmux-in-tmux muscle memory.
241	2. **Rebind the inner herdr prefix.** Set `keys.prefix` (e.g. `"ctrl+a"` / `"ctrl+space"`) so the inner herdr uses a non-colliding prefix — one keystroke instead of the double-tap. Cost: it changes herdr's prefix even when run standalone (no longer matching tmux's `Ctrl+b`).
242	3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
243	
244	Notes: this repo's tmux uses many root-table `bind -n C-*` bindings that **shadow** inner-app `Ctrl` keys, so herdr's prefix-free *direct* terminal shortcuts aren't reliable under tmux — reach herdr actions through its prefix (via 1 or 2). herdr's own `allow_nested` (config, default `false`) governs herdr-inside-**herdr** only (detected via `HERDR_ENV`), not herdr-inside-tmux.
245	
246	## Review-pending flag (mark-unread / ⭐)
247	
248	The tmux setup has a per-window bookmark (`@bookmark_status` + `toggle-bookmark.sh`, rendered via `#{?@bookmark_status,…}`). herdr has **no `#{@option}` status-bar interpolation**, so that exact mechanism doesn't port — but the *use case* that actually matters here does: **"the agent finished (`done`) but I haven't reviewed it yet."** herdr collapses a `done` pane to `idle` the moment you peek in, losing the only signal that it still needs attention.
249	
250	The fix uses herdr's **per-pane custom-status metadata**, which is orthogonal to native agent detection:
251	
252	```bash
253	herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --custom-status "⭐ REVIEW"   # set (persistent — no --ttl-ms)
254	herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --clear-custom-status         # clear
255	```
256	
257	Verified: a pane can carry `custom_status:"⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking in does **not** wipe the flag (the whole point). `herdr pane get` surfaces the `custom_status` field and `herdr pane list` (native JSON — **no** `--json` flag) lets the inbox enumerate flagged panes, so there is **no sidecar file**; herdr itself is the source of truth.
258	
259	Surfaces (all sharing one script, `~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh` = `dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh` — the analog of tmux's `toggle-bookmark.sh`):
260	
261	| Surface | Action |
262	|---|---|
263	| `hmark` / `hunmark` (aliases in `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`) | set / clear on the current pane (ambient `$HERDR_PANE_ID`), or pass a pane id |
264	| `prefix+m` | toggle the flag on the focused pane (uses `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`) |
265	| `tv herdr-review` / `prefix+i` | the **inbox**: lists only flagged panes. `Enter` focuses & **keeps** the ⭐ (you may still be mid-review); `Alt+C` focuses **and** clears it ("mark read") |
266	
267	**Caveat — `custom_status` is a single value per pane.** The deferred usage-status driver (below) also pushes `--custom-status`; although it uses a different `--source`, `herdr pane get` exposes one flattened `custom_status`, so the two would contend for the visible label. No live conflict today (the usage driver isn't built and review flags are short-lived), but see [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
268	
269	## AI usage / quota status
270	
271	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into (the same hook the **Review-pending flag** section above uses — note both write the single per-pane `custom_status`). A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
272	
273	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
274	
275	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
276	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
277	- **Decorative status-bar glyphs** (📌/🔖 as free-floating window labels): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation, so tmux-style status-bar bookmarks don't port. *(The specific "mark-unread / review-pending ⭐" use case IS solved — see the **Review-pending flag** section above — via per-pane `custom_status` metadata; only the purely decorative status-bar glyph remains a gap.)*
278	- **Per-key pane resize.** tmux binds `prefix+H/J/K/L` (and `M-hjkl` for fine steps) to resize directly; herdr has no per-key resize — it uses a modal `resize_mode` (`prefix+r`), then `h/j/k/l`. Not exact parity, but a close analog.
279	
280	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
281	
282	## See also
283

285	- [Tool managers — where tools come from](../this_repo/tool-managers.md)

2	# https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr
3	#
4	# herdr-native analogs of the sesh/tmux helpers in 22_sesh.sh. herdr's model is
5	# Workspace -> Tab -> Pane (tmux is Session -> Window -> Pane), and its CLI
6	# (`herdr workspace|tab|pane|agent …`) is the scripting surface that replaces
7	# `tmux new-session/split-window`.
8	#
9	# Backend that powers the user-facing commands and their aliases:
10	#   herdr-vibe / hvibe  — parametric multi-agent pack in a new workspace
11	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit tab + nvim tab)
12	#   herdr-code / hcode  — repo-scoped single-agent layout
13	#                         (nvim | agent split + btop monitor tab)
14	#
15	# REUSE: the *pure* (multiplexer-agnostic) helpers from 22_sesh.sh are reused
16	# verbatim — `_sesh_git_root`, `_sesh_sanitize`, `_sesh_wrap_agent` (specstory
17	# wrapping), `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` (shell|kill|restart post-exit behavior).
18	# 22_sesh.sh sorts before this file, so they are defined by the time hvibe/hcode
19	# run. Only the tmux calls are swapped for `herdr …` CLI calls.
20	#
21	# Bash baseline: 4+ (same array-slicing idiom as svibe; no `local -A`).

28	# Echo the workspace_id of an existing workspace whose label == $1 (else empty).
29	# Used for idempotency: re-running hvibe/hcode in a repo focuses the existing
30	# workspace instead of stacking duplicates (mirrors svibe's has-session check).
31	function _herdr_ws_by_label() {
32	    herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null \
33	        | jq -r --arg l "$1" '.result.workspaces[]? | select(.label==$l) | .workspace_id' 2>/dev/null \
34	        | head -1
35	}
36	
37	# Compose the shell command for one agent pane: specstory-wrap then on-exit-wrap.
38	# $1=agent  $2=specstory_mode(auto|never)  $3=on_exit(shell|kill|restart)
39	function _herdr_agent_cmd() {
40	    local inner
41	    inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$2")
42	    _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$3" "${1:-agent}"
43	}
44	
45	# Create a labeled tab in workspace $1 (cwd $2, label $3) and run command $4 in
46	# its root pane. `tab create` returns the new pane id at .result.root_pane.
47	# $1=workspace_id  $2=cwd  $3=label  $4=command
48	function _herdr_tool_tab() {
49	    local pane
50	    pane=$(herdr tab create --workspace "$1" --cwd "$2" --label "$3" --no-focus 2>/dev/null \
51	        | jq -r '.result.root_pane.pane_id // empty')
52	    [ -n "$pane" ] && herdr pane run "$pane" "$4" >/dev/null 2>&1
53	}

55	# Resolve the target herdr session for hvibe/hcode from an optional --session
56	# value. Echoes "<name><TAB><socket_override_or_empty>". The socket field is
57	# non-empty ONLY when the caller must override HERDR_SOCKET_PATH (explicit
58	# --session); empty means "use the ambient/default socket untouched". Returns 1
59	# (with a message) when an explicit --session names a session that isn't running.
60	#
61	# A herdr server hosts multiple named sessions (default + `herdr --session NAME`),
62	# each with its own socket. The CLI has no --session flag on subcommands; the
63	# only lever is the HERDR_SOCKET_PATH env var (verified). `session list --json`
64	# is the authoritative name -> socket_path resolver.
65	function _herdr_session_target() {
66	    local want="$1" js line running socket nm
67	    js=$(herdr session list --json 2>/dev/null)
68	    if [ -n "$want" ]; then
69	        line=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
70	            | jq -r --arg n "$want" '.sessions[] | select(.name==$n) | "\(.running)\t\(.socket_path)"' 2>/dev/null \
71	            | head -1)
72	        if [ -z "$line" ]; then
73	            echo "session '$want' not found. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
74	            return 1
75	        fi
76	        running=${line%%$'\t'*}
77	        socket=${line#*$'\t'}
78	        if [ "$running" != "true" ]; then
79	            echo "session '$want' is not running. Start it with: herdr --session $want" >&2
80	            return 1
81	        fi
82	        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$want" "$socket"
83	        return 0
84	    fi
85	    # No explicit --session: inside herdr use the ambient session (no override);
86	    # outside, fall back to the default session. Only the NAME matters here (for
87	    # the attach path) — socket stays empty so the ambient socket is left as-is.
88	    if [ -n "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" ]; then
89	        nm=$(printf '%s' "$js" \
90	            | jq -r --arg s "$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH" '.sessions[] | select(.socket_path==$s) | .name' 2>/dev/null \
91	            | head -1)
92	        printf '%s\t\n' "${nm:-default}"
93	    else
94	        printf 'default\t\n'
95	    fi
96	}

98	# When hvibe/hcode run from OUTSIDE herdr, bring up a client attached to the
99	# session so the just-created/focused workspace is actually visible — the
100	# `herdr workspace focus` calls only move an ALREADY-attached client. Inside
101	# herdr (HERDR_ENV set) those focus calls already switched the live client, so
102	# there is nothing to do. Runs the client as a child (no exec), mirroring
103	# svibe's `tmux attach-session`. $1=session_name (default: "default").
104	function _herdr_attach_if_outside() {
105	    [ -n "$HERDR_ENV" ] && return 0
106	    local session="${1:-default}"
107	    if [ "$session" = "default" ]; then
108	        herdr
109	    else
110	        herdr session attach "$session"
111	    fi
112	}

412	            -h|--help)
413	                cat <<'EOF'
414	hcode — herdr single-agent coding layout (herdr analog of scode)
415	
416	Usage: hcode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
417	             [--no-attach] [--session NAME] [AGENT]
418	
419	Builds a new herdr workspace `coding-agent/<repo>`:
420	  tab "editor"  — nvim (left ~75%) | agent (right ~25%)
421	  tab "monitor" — btop (or htop / top)

2	# ~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Set / clear / toggle a per-pane "review-pending" flag on a herdr pane, using
6	# herdr's per-pane custom-status metadata (`herdr pane report-metadata … --source
7	# review --custom-status …`). This is the herdr analog of tmux's
8	# `@bookmark_status` (dot_config/tmux/executable_toggle-bookmark.sh) — the
9	# problem it solves is the SAME: keep a session visibly flagged as "I still need
10	# to review this" even after the agent's own state flips to idle.
11	#
12	# Why custom-status and not agent state: it is pushed under a dedicated
13	# `--source review`, ORTHOGONAL to herdr's native agent detection. Verified: a
14	# pane can carry `custom_status:"⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so
15	# peeking into a done pane (which collapses it to idle) does NOT wipe the flag.
16	# Omitting --ttl-ms makes it persistent (no auto-expiry).
17	#
18	# The single source of truth for the mark IS herdr itself: `herdr pane get`
19	# surfaces the `custom_status` field, and `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO
20	# --json flag) lets the `tv herdr-review` inbox enumerate flagged panes. No
21	# sidecar file.
22	#
23	# Usage:
24	#   review-mark.sh set    <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # default "⭐ REVIEW"
25	#   review-mark.sh clear  <pane_id>
26	#   review-mark.sh toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]   # clear if flagged, else set
27	#
28	# Consumers: hmark/hunmark (dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh), the prefix+m keybind
29	# (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), and the herdr-review tv channel's
30	# focus_clear action. Keep the marker MATCH substring ("REVIEW") in sync with
31	# that channel's jq filter (dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml).
32	set -eu
33	
34	SOURCE_ID='review'
35	MATCH='REVIEW'                 # substring the tv channel filters on (glyph-agnostic)
36	DEFAULT_STATUS='⭐ REVIEW'
37	
38	usage() {
39	    printf 'usage: %s set|clear|toggle <pane_id> [glyph-text]\n' "$0" >&2
40	    exit 64
41	}
42	
43	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
44	
45	action="${1:-}"
46	pane="${2:-}"
47	status="${3:-$DEFAULT_STATUS}"
48	
49	[ -n "$action" ] || usage
50	[ -n "$pane" ] || usage
51	
52	_set() {
53	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --custom-status "$status" >/dev/null
54	    echo "review flag set on $pane"
55	}
56	
57	_clear() {
58	    herdr pane report-metadata "$pane" --source "$SOURCE_ID" --clear-custom-status >/dev/null
59	    echo "review flag cleared on $pane"
60	}
61	
62	case "$action" in
63	    set)   _set ;;
64	    clear) _clear ;;
65	    toggle)
66	        command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "review-mark: jq is required for toggle" >&2; exit 1; }
67	        current=$(herdr pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null \
68	            | jq -r '.result.pane.custom_status // ""' 2>/dev/null || true)
69	        case "$current" in
70	            *"$MATCH"*) _clear ;;
71	            *)          _set ;;
72	        esac ;;
73	    *) usage ;;
74	esac

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# ~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh
3	# Source: dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh (managed by chezmoi)
4	#
5	# Open a NEW TAB rooted at the WORKSPACE ("space") directory, NOT the focused
6	# pane's live cwd.
7	#
8	# Why this exists: on herdr >=0.7.x, `new_cwd = "follow"` makes a new tab inherit
9	# the FOCUSED pane's cwd — herdr issue #912 (https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912)
10	# changed `follow` so new tabs behave like pane splits, and the older "new tab
11	# opens at the workspace's initial dir" was treated as a bug and removed. There
12	# is NO new_cwd value for "workspace dir", so we compute it and pass it via
13	# `herdr tab create --cwd`. (herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field either —
14	# `herdr workspace get` has no cwd — so it must be derived.)
15	#
16	# "Space dir" = the workspace's ROOT tab's pane cwd, where the root tab is the
17	# lowest-numbered tab — the one whose live-cwd basename herdr uses as the
18	# workspace label. We prefer the live cwd (foreground_cwd, matches the label),
19	# falling back to the shell startup cwd.
20	#
21	# Bound to prefix+C (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml). prefix+c and the mouse
22	# "+" button keep herdr's native follow-the-focused-pane behavior. Uses the
23	# keybind-context $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID (falls back to ambient $HERDR_PANE_ID).
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   new-tab-at-space-root.sh [pane_id]   # pane_id defaults to the current pane
27	set -eu
28	
29	command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: herdr not found" >&2; exit 1; }
30	command -v jq    >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
31	
32	pane="${1:-${HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID:-${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}}}"
33	[ -n "$pane" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: no pane id (pass one, or run inside herdr)" >&2; exit 64; }
34	
35	wid=$(herdr pane get "$pane" | jq -r '.result.pane.workspace_id // ""')
36	[ -n "$wid" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: could not resolve workspace for pane $pane" >&2; exit 1; }
37	
38	# Root tab = lowest tab number in the workspace (herdr labels the space after it).
39	root_tab=$(herdr tab list --workspace "$wid" | jq -r '.result.tabs | sort_by(.number) | .[0].tab_id // ""')
40	[ -n "$root_tab" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: no tabs in workspace $wid" >&2; exit 1; }
41	
42	# `herdr tab get` returns tab metadata only (no pane cwd), so read the root tab's
43	# pane cwd from the full pane list. Prefer live cwd so it matches the space label.
44	root=$(herdr pane list | jq -r --arg t "$root_tab" \
45	    '.result.panes | map(select(.tab_id==$t)) | .[0] // {} | (.foreground_cwd // .cwd // "")')
46	[ -n "$root" ] || { echo "new-tab-at-space-root: could not resolve root dir for $root_tab" >&2; exit 1; }
47	
48	exec herdr tab create --workspace "$wid" --cwd "$root" --focus
49
```
</details></tool-use>

Show herdr tv channel configs

`for f in herdr-sesh herdr-agent-panes herdr-review; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat /home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/$f.toml; done`

```text
===== herdr-sesh =====
# Session/workspace switcher cable channel for herdr (tv) — sesh analog
#
# herdr-native counterpart of the tmux-coupled `sesh.toml` channel. `sesh`
# manages tmux sessions, so it does not apply under herdr; this channel switches
# herdr WORKSPACES (the project-level unit) and opens new ones from zoxide
# frecency dirs. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+T` in
# ~/.config/herdr/config.toml). See docs/tools/herdr.md.
#
# Sources (cycle with Ctrl+S):
#   1. Existing herdr workspaces  → Enter = `herdr workspace focus <id>`
#   2. zoxide frecency dirs        → Enter = `herdr workspace create --cwd <dir>`
#
# TSV columns: 0 = kind (ws|dir), 1 = ref (workspace_id|path), 2 = display.

[metadata]
name = "herdr-sesh"
description = "herdr workspace switcher + zoxide dir opener (herdr-aware sesh analog)"
requirements = ["herdr", "jq", "zoxide"]

[source]
command = [
  '''herdr workspace list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.workspaces[]? | "ws\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.label)  (\(.pane_count)p, \(.tab_count)t)"' ''',
  '''zoxide query -l 2>/dev/null | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}{print "dir",$0,$0}' ''',
]
display = "{split:\t:2}"
output = "{split:\t:1}"

[preview]
command = '''
kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
case "$kind" in
  ws)
    printf '\033[1mworkspace %s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
    herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null | jq . 2>/dev/null \
      || herdr workspace get "$ref" 2>/dev/null
    ;;
  dir)
    printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m\n\n' "$ref"
    if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then eza -la --git --color=always "$ref" 2>/dev/null
    else ls -la "$ref" 2>/dev/null; fi
    ;;
esac
'''

[ui]
input_header = "herdr Workspaces / Dirs"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open"
ctrl-d = ["actions:close_ws", "reload_source"]

[actions.open]
description = "Focus the workspace, or open a new workspace at the directory"
command = '''
kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
[ -z "$ref" ] && exit 0
case "$kind" in
  ws)  herdr workspace focus "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
  dir) herdr workspace create --cwd "$ref" --focus >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
esac
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.close_ws]
description = "Close the selected herdr workspace"
command = '''
kind='{split:\t:0}'; ref='{split:\t:1}'
[ "$kind" = "ws" ] && [ -n "$ref" ] && herdr workspace close "$ref" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"
===== herdr-agent-panes =====
# Live agent panes cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware variant
#
# herdr-native counterpart of `agent-panes.toml` (which is tmux-coupled). Lists
# panes from the running herdr server and lets you jump to the one running an
# agent. Use under herdr (bound to `prefix+A` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml).
#
# herdr has no "focus pane by id" command (pane focus is directional only), so
# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB (`herdr workspace focus` +
# `herdr tab focus`) — tab-level granularity, which is enough when there's one
# agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
#
# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` via jq:
#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
#   3. agent_status   (working / idle / blocked / unknown)
#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)

[metadata]
name = "herdr-agent-panes"
description = "Live panes across the herdr server — jump to a running agent's workspace/tab"
requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]

[source]
command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.agent_status)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
display = "{split:\t:0}  [{split:\t:3}]  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
output = "{split:\t:0}"

[preview]
command = '''
pane='{split:\t:0}'
printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  [%s]\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
'''

[ui]
input_header = "Live herdr Agent Panes"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:focus"
alt-t = "actions:focus"
alt-k = "actions:close_pane"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"

[actions.focus]
description = "Jump to the pane's workspace + tab"
command = '''
ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.close_pane]
description = "Close the pane (confirm prompt)"
command = '''
p='{split:\t:0}'
[ -z "$p" ] && exit 0
printf 'Close pane %s? [y/N] ' "$p"
read -r ans
case "$ans" in
  y|Y|yes|YES) herdr pane close "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "closed $p" || echo "failed (already gone?)" ;;
  *) echo "aborted" ;;
esac
echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _
'''
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy_id]
description = "Copy pane id to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:0}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_dir]
description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:4}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"
===== herdr-review =====
# Review-pending inbox cable channel for herdr (tv) — herdr-aware
#
# Lists herdr panes carrying a "review-pending" flag (⭐) — the ones whose agent
# finished but you haven't reviewed yet. Companion to `herdr-agent-panes.toml`;
# the flag is set by hmark / prefix+m (see dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh)
# and stored as the pane's `custom_status` metadata, orthogonal to agent state.
# Bound to `prefix+i` in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Enter jumps to the pane's WORKSPACE + TAB but KEEPS the ⭐ (you may still be
# mid-review). Alt+C = focus AND clear the flag ("mark read"). herdr has no
# "focus pane by id" (pane focus is directional only), so we focus at tab
# granularity — enough with one agent per tab. See docs/tools/herdr.md.
#
# Source: TSV from `herdr pane list` (native JSON, NO --json flag) via jq,
# filtered to panes whose custom_status contains "REVIEW" (glyph-agnostic; keep
# in sync with the MATCH substring in review-mark.sh):
#   0. pane_id        (w1:p1)
#   1. workspace_id   (w1)
#   2. tab_id         (w1:t1)
#   3. custom_status  (⭐ REVIEW)
#   4. cwd            (foreground cwd, falling back to pane cwd)

[metadata]
name = "herdr-review"
description = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐) — jump to sessions you flagged for later"
requirements = ["herdr", "jq"]

[source]
command = '''herdr pane list 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.panes[]? | select(.custom_status? // "" | test("REVIEW")) | "\(.pane_id)\t\(.workspace_id)\t\(.tab_id)\t\(.custom_status)\t\(.foreground_cwd // .cwd)"' '''
display = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:3}  {split:\t:4|split:/:-1}"
output = "{split:\t:0}"

[preview]
command = '''
pane='{split:\t:0}'
printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  %s\n' "$pane" '{split:\t:3}'
printf '\033[2mworkspace:\033[0m %s   \033[2mtab:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:1}' '{split:\t:2}'
printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n' '{split:\t:4}'
printf '\n\033[1m─── pane (herdr pane read, last ~80) ───\033[0m\n'
herdr pane read "$pane" --source visible --lines 80 2>/dev/null \
  || echo "(pane $pane no longer exists — press Ctrl+R to reload)"
'''

[ui]
input_header = "Review-pending herdr panes (⭐)"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:focus"
alt-t = "actions:focus"
alt-c = ["actions:focus_clear", "reload_source"]
ctrl-y = "actions:copy_id"
alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"

[actions.focus]
description = "Jump to the pane's workspace + tab (keep the ⭐)"
command = '''
ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.focus_clear]
description = "Jump to the pane AND clear the ⭐ (mark read)"
command = '''
pane='{split:\t:0}'; ws='{split:\t:1}'; tab='{split:\t:2}'
[ -n "$ws" ] && herdr workspace focus "$ws" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$tab" ] && herdr tab focus "$tab" >/dev/null 2>&1
[ -n "$pane" ] && "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/herdr/review-mark.sh" clear "$pane" >/dev/null 2>&1
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_id]
description = "Copy pane id to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:0}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy_dir]
description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
command = '''
d='{split:\t:4}'
[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
fi
'''
mode = "fork"
```

```text
1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
5	# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
6	# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
7	# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
8	# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
9	# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
10	# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
11	#
12	# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
13	# new contents on stdout.
14	#
15	# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
16	#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
17	#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
18	#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
19	#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
20	#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
21	#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
22	#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
23	#
24	# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
25	# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
26	# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
27	# round-trips both.
28	#
29	# Note: the template is written to a temp file via a heredoc *redirect* (not
30	# captured with $(...)), because the config body contains a lone backtick
31	# (`key = "prefix+\`"`) that bash mis-parses as command substitution when a
32	# quoted heredoc is nested inside $(...). Passing the path to Python sidesteps it.
33	#
34	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
35	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
36	# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
37	# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
38	# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
39	set -eu
40	
41	tmpl_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/herdr-config.XXXXXX")
42	trap 'rm -f "$tmpl_file"' EXIT INT TERM
43	
44	cat <<'TOML' > "$tmpl_file"
45	{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
46	TOML
47	
48	live=$(cat)
49	
50	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
51	  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -
52	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	  set -- python3 -
54	else
55	  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; emitting managed template" >&2
56	  cat "$tmpl_file"
57	  exit 0
58	fi
59	
60	HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE="$tmpl_file" HERDR_LIVE="$live" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
61	import os
62	import sys
63	
64	tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
65	with open(tmpl_path, "r") as fh:
66	    template_text = fh.read()
67	
68	
69	def emit_template():
70	    sys.stdout.write(template_text)
71	
72	
73	# Read side: stdlib tomllib (uv guarantees >=3.11); tomli backport otherwise.
74	try:
75	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
76	except ModuleNotFoundError:
77	    try:
78	        import tomli as tomllib
79	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
80	        # No TOML reader → can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is
81	        # (loses runtime-key preservation, but keeps the host configured).
82	        emit_template()
83	        sys.exit(0)
84	
85	# Write side: tomlkit preserves comments + array-of-tables. uv installs it via
86	# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.
87	try:
88	    import tomlkit
89	except ModuleNotFoundError:
90	    print(
91	        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
92	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
93	        file=sys.stderr,
94	    )
95	    emit_template()
96	    sys.exit(0)
97	
98	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
99	
100	live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()
101	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
102	live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
103	
104	# Pull through every top-level key herdr owns at runtime that we don't manage.
105	for key, value in live.items():
106	    if key in MANAGED or key in doc:
107	        continue
108	    doc[key] = value
109	
110	sys.stdout.write(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
111	PYEOF
112
```
</details></tool-use>

10	# below on every `chezmoi apply` and preserves any keys herdr writes back at
11	# runtime (onboarding / [session] / [remote] / [update] / [experimental]).
12	#

19	#
20	# Prefix is ctrl+b (herdr default, same as tmux). herdr's built-in defaults are
21	# already close to tmux (prefix+c new tab, prefix+1..9 switch, prefix+h/j/k/l
22	# focus pane, prefix+v / prefix+minus split, prefix+z zoom, prefix+x close,
23	# prefix+g session navigator, prefix+w workspace nav, prefix+q detach), so we
24	# only rebind a couple of keys and add command panes for the tv/lazygit popups.

26	[theme]

40	shell_mode = "auto"           # login/non-login auto-detect; follows $SHELL
41	# CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces (no explicit --cwd). Values:
42	#   "follow"  = inherit the SOURCE pane/workspace (default)
43	#   "home"    = $HOME · "current" = herdr's own process dir · or a fixed path
44	# NOTE (herdr >=0.7.x): with "follow", a NEW TAB inherits the FOCUSED pane's live

47	# removed. NO new_cwd value opens a new tab at the WORKSPACE ("space") dir — for
48	# that use the prefix+C command below (derives the space root → tab create --cwd).
49	# See docs/tools/herdr.md.

51	
52	# --- Built-in action rebinds (tmux muscle memory) ---
53	# Only existing actions can be rebound; we keep herdr defaults for everything
54	# not listed here. An action accepts an ARRAY of bindings (herdr docs), so a
55	# single action can carry both the intuitive key and the tmux-default key.
56	[keys]
57	split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]         # side-by-side (left/right) = tmux prefix+| and prefix+% (-h)
58	split_horizontal = ["prefix+minus", "prefix+\""]  # stacked (top/bottom)      = tmux prefix+- and prefix+" (-v)
59	reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"   # tmux: prefix+R
60	rename_tab = "prefix+,"            # tmux: prefix+, (rename window) — frees prefix+shift+t for the sesh popup below
61	new_worktree = "prefix+shift+b"    # moved off prefix+shift+g so prefix+G can be lazygit (worktrees handled by wt/wm + herdr-plus auto-layout)
62	
63	# --- Indexed quick-switch (native herdr actions) ---
64	# switch_tab (prefix+1..9) is a herdr built-in; add the workspace + agent analogs
65	# so a number key jumps directly, no navigate mode needed. The "N..M" range form
66	# is native herdr config syntax (same shape as switch_tab).
67	# NOTE on the modifier: prefix+SHIFT+digit does NOT work — under the kitty
68	# keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) shift+1 still carries the printable "!", so
69	# herdr matches the symbol, not "shift+1". ctrl+digit and alt+digit have no
70	# printable form, so they disambiguate cleanly. Hence ctrl (workspace) / alt (agent).
71	switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"    # prefix+ctrl+N → workspace N (shift+N would emit !@#… — unusable)
72	focus_agent = "prefix+alt+1..9"          # prefix+alt+N  → jump to agent N's pane (herdr tracks agents per pane natively)

77	# hjkl muscle memory carries here too. (These fields can't use prefix+/enter/tab/
78	# left/right or unmodified 1-9 — plain j/k are allowed.)
79	navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
80	navigate_workspace_up = ["k", "up"]

83	# type = "pane": opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits —
84	# herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. The command runs from the focused
85	# pane's cwd and gets $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH / $HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID /

```text
Exit code 2
## Quick Actions

A fuzzy launcher for one-off commands. Trigger it (action
`cloudmanic.herdr-plus.quick-actions`), fuzzy-pick an action, and it runs in the
directory you launched from. Actions are TOML files in the `quick-actions/` subdir
of [herdr-plus's config dir](#configuration) (seeded with editable examples on
first run). A repo can also ship its own in `<repo>/.herdr-plus/quick-actions/`, shown
under a **Project** heading above your **Global** ones — this repo ships
`make build` / `make test` as a live example.

There are three action types:

```toml
# command (default) — runs immediately
name = "GitHub"
command = "open https://github.com"
```

```toml
# select — pick from a second fuzzy list; the choice becomes {{.Value}}
name = "Open Repo"
type = "select"
command = "open https://github.com/cloudmanic/{{.Value}}"

[[options]]
label = "Herdr Plus"
value = "herdr-plus"
```

```toml
# form — type a value that becomes {{.Value}}
name = "Search Google"
type = "form"
command = "open 'https://www.google.com/search?q={{.Value | urlquery}}'"

[form]
prompt = "Search Google for"
```

The `command` is a [Go template](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template) rendered against
the launch context: `{{.WorkDir}}` (where you launched from), `{{.SessionTitle}}`
(the workspace label), `{{.Value}}` (select/form input), and more — also exported
as `HERDR_PLUS_*` environment variables. If a command doesn't reference
`{{.Value}}`, the value is appended as a final shell-quoted argument.

## Worktree auto-layout

herdr-plus can lay a project-style tab layout into a git **worktree** the moment
herdr creates *or opens* it. When you run `herdr worktree create`/`open` (or use
herdr's right-click worktree dialog), herdr makes a fresh workspace for the
worktree and fires a `worktree.created` event (new worktree) or `worktree.opened`
event (existing one); herdr-plus catches either, finds a layout matching the
worktree's repo, and opens that layout's tabs and panes in the new workspace —
every command running — with no keypress. This is the plugin system's `[[events]]`
hook (declared in [`herdr-plugin.toml`](herdr-plugin.toml)) put to work.

Layouts live in `~/.config/herdr-plus/worktrees/`, one TOML file per layout (the
file name doesn't matter). A layout is a `repo` matcher plus the same `[[tabs]]`
format projects use:

```toml
repo = "options-cafe"          # matches the worktree's repo name (case-insensitive)

[[tabs]]
name = "claude"
command = "claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --chrome"

[[tabs]]
name = "lazygit"
command = "lazygit"

[[tabs]]
name = "terminal"              # no command — just an empty shell
```

- **`repo`** (required) matches the new worktree's repository name — the repo's
  basename, e.g. `options-cafe` — case-insensitively.
- **`branch`** (optional) narrows a layout to worktrees created on exactly that
  branch. When more than one layout matches, a branch-specific one wins over a
  repo-only one.
- **`[[tabs]]`** is identical to a project's tabs, including multi-pane
  `[[tabs.panes]]` splits (see [Split panes within a tab](#split-panes-within-a-tab)).

### Turning a layout on and off

The switch is simply **whether the file exists**. A layout in `worktrees/` is on;
to turn one off, delete the file (or move it out of the directory). With no files
in `worktrees/` at all, the feature is inert — every worktree fires the event, and
herdr-plus does nothing when nothing matches.

The handler's output shows up in `herdr plugin log list --plugin
cloudmanic.herdr-plus`, so you can confirm whether a layout fired.

## Binding a key

Binding keys to the actions is an optional, one-time edit to **your** herdr
`config.toml` (`~/.config/herdr/config.toml`). Add `[[keys.command]]` entries with
`type = "plugin_action"` whose `command` is the action id:

```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+up"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.projects"
description = "herdr-plus: projects"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+down"
type = "plugin_action"
===== global quick-actions dir contents =====
```

# herdr — research report

## 1. What herdr IS

**herdr is a Rust terminal multiplexer with built-in AI-coding-agent awareness** — a tmux/zellij competitor that is *mouse-first* and *agent-native*. Upstream: `github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr`, docs at `herdr.dev/docs`. It tracks per-pane agent state (idle / working / blocked / done) and rolls it up into a sidebar.

In this repo it's shipped as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** (you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, not nested by default). Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes — herdr is purely additive.

Stated verbatim at the top of the config: *"Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator."*

## 2. All herdr files in the repo

**Config (the managed body + overlay mechanism):**
- `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` — the **managed config body** (the real content).
- `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` — a chezmoi **`modify_` overlay** script (POSIX sh + embedded Python). It enforces the `[theme]`/`[ui]`/`[terminal]`/`[keys]` tables on every `chezmoi apply` while *pulling through* any top-level keys herdr writes back at runtime (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`). Uses `uv run --with tomlkit` (falls back to system `python3`, then to emitting the raw template). Was previously a `create_` seed-once file; switched to `modify_` so repo edits reach already-seeded hosts.

**Helper scripts (chezmoi `executable_`):**
